footnotes: The 2025 tax provision includes a one-time non-cash charge recorded in Q3 2025, which lowered net income and EPS.
Free cash flow as reported by Meta: operating cash flow − purchases of property & equipment − principal payments on finance leases.
Diluted EPS by quarter as reported in the 10-Qs; fourth quarters are calculated (net income ÷ estimated diluted shares) because EPS does not add across quarters.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Meta's revenue grew 22.2% to $201.0B in 2025, driven by advertising, where ad impressions rose 12% and average price per ad 9%. Operating income rose 20.0% to $83.3B as Family of Apps earned $102.5B and Reality Labs lost $19.2B.

Net income dipped 3.1% to $60.5B, or $23.49 per diluted share, because the tax provision tripled to $25.5B, including a one-time non-cash charge of about $15.9B in Q3. Capital spending nearly doubled to $69.7B, so free cash flow fell 16.3% to $43.6B.
highlights: Q4 2025 revenue reached a record $59.9B, up 24% from a year earlier.
Family of Apps operating income grew 17.6% to $102.5B.
Family daily active people reached 3.58 billion in December 2025, up 7%.
watch: Capital expenditures rose 87% to $69.7B, and the 2026 outlook calls for $115B–$135B.
Long-term debt doubled to $58.7B, cutting net cash to $22.8B from $49.0B.
Reality Labs' operating loss widened to $19.2B from $17.7B.
R&D expense rose 30.8% to $57.4B, and 2026 total expenses are guided to $162B–$169B.
